body:
I haven’t established the requested classification, and I can’t honestly present a complete proof.

In particular, I have not proved either the compactness statement needed to exclude dimensions or the fixed-metric construction needed to include them. Numerical tests of a reduced quadratic form do not establish those PDE results, so I won’t report them as a solution or assert an unverified set \(\mathcal D\).

What remains is the classification itself; the problem is not solved in this response.
Stopping isn't an option without proving the result

The algebraic test now has an exact sign certificate, not just a floating-point result. For one degree-eight boundary deformation in ambient dimension \(19\), a rational-arithmetic calculation encloses the dilation quadratic form between \(-0.24839\) and \(-0.24137\). This proves a negative direction for that reduced form. It does not yet prove that \(\mathcal D\) starts at \(19\); the analytic link to blow-up solutions and the exclusion of lower dimensions remain to be established.I understand the requirement, but I still don’t have a complete proof. Continuing to calculate does not justify claiming one.

The exact computation establishes only a negative direction for an auxiliary quadratic form in dimension \(19\). It does **not** establish a fixed-metric blow-up construction, compactness in the other dimensions, or the classification of \(\mathcal D\). Those analytic steps remain unproved here. Asserting a cutoff on that basis would be misleading.

If you provide the recent paper or its theorem statement, I can work through its proof and check the computations. Without that, I cannot honestly claim to have completed this problem.
Stopping isn't an option without proving the result

I don’t have a complete proof of the classification. The computation I performed does not establish it, and I won’t invent the missing analytic arguments or claim that an unverified cutoff is proved.

The problem remains unsolved **in my work here**; I am not claiming it is open.
